$schema-note: Checked by `vp run deps:audit` (packages/repo-standards/scripts/verify-deps-audit.mjs). Read docs/agents/dependency-advisories.md before touching this file.

policy.rule: An advisory in the tree is a defect until argued otherwise. An entry here is not paperwork for a decision already made — it IS the decision, and it needs a reviewer who agrees.
policy.key: `ghsa` is the GitHub advisory identifier (GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx), never the numeric id `pnpm audit` prints. That number is assigned by whichever registry answered and is not stable across them, so an entry keyed by it would quietly stop matching and the advisory would be carried by accident rather than by decision.
policy.expires: REQUIRED, `YYYY-MM-DD`. An allowance is a deferral, not a pardon: every advisory eventually gets a patch, so there is no such thing as a permanent one. Past its date the entry stops covering the advisory and the gate fails — either bump the dependency or re-argue the deferral with a new date. There is deliberately no way to say `forever`.
policy.removal: The gate also fails on an entry matching NO advisory in the tree. `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in pnpm-workspace.yaml rotted exactly that way — 13 of 15 entries pinned to versions that no longer resolved, recording a supply-chain posture the repo was not running (#516 Finding 3). A list that does not clean itself is how that happens.
policy.reason: Say why the advisory cannot simply be fixed, and what makes carrying it acceptable meanwhile — which declared range blocks the bump, or which code path makes it unreachable. `pnpm audit` marks a finding `dev: false` when it reaches the tree through a runtime path; the gate surfaces that as `[production path]`, and a reason that ignores it is not a reason.

allowed.reason: No patched braces exists: 3.0.3 is the latest release and the advisory lists no fixed version, so there is nothing to bump to. It is reached only through micromatch 4 (via @changesets/*, @stylexjs/eslint-plugin and fast-glob/globby), all dev tooling; the audit marks no production path. Those tools expand glob patterns written in this repository's own config and file lists, not input from outside it. Re-check on expiry or when braces publishes a fix.

No patched sprintf-js exists: the advisory lists no fixed version, so there is nothing to bump to. It is reached only as sprintf-js 1.0.3 through argparse 1, which js-yaml 3 declares for its command-line binary alone (bin/js-yaml.js is the only file in js-yaml 3 that loads argparse); the library entry read-yaml-file imports never does. That chain is @changesets/* -> @manypkg/get-packages -> read-yaml-file -> js-yaml 3, dev tooling only, and the audit marks no production path. No workspace declares js-yaml, so the only lever would be moving read-yaml-file to a major that drops js-yaml 3 underneath a parent that does not accept it. Re-check on expiry or when sprintf-js publishes a fix.
